ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Here is a graph that shows a growth curve for a population of bacteria. Calculate the mean rate of population growth between day 2 and day 4. Give your answer to the nearest whole number.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a bacterial population growth curve, with the horizontal axis as Time (days) and the vertical axis as Population (thousands). Reading from the curve, at day 2 the population is about 20 thousand, and at day 4 the population is about 80 thousand. Reasoning: The average growth rate equals the amount of population change divided by the amount of time change, namely (80 - 20) thousand / (4 - 2) days = 60 thousand / 2 days = 30 thousand bacteria per day. Converted to an ordinary number, this is 30,000 bacteria per day, and taking the nearest integer is still 30000.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify the population at day 2 as 20 thousand and at day 4 as 80 thousand. From the question text, use the interval day 2 to day 4 and give a whole-number rate. Compute the mean growth rate: (80 - 20) thousand / (4 - 2) days = 60 thousand / 2 = 30 thousand bacteria per day, which is 30000.
